body:
Title: Docs: add workload-aware batching tiers (fast/standard/cost-efficient) + FAQ and migration guidance

Context
We’re rolling out workload-aware batching defaults (tiered profiles) behind a feature flag as part of runtime-1.21. Customers need clear guidance on: (1) what the tiers mean, (2) how to set them per route/model, (3) how they interact with explicit batching overrides, and (4) what to monitor when changing tiers (latency tail, timeouts, streaming cadence).

This PR adds the customer-facing docs pages + updates existing config reference pages to include batching_tier and links to the FAQ/troubleshooting section. It also addresses support feedback (SUP-18510) requesting clearer explanation of “tier vs knobs” and a way to view “effective config”.

What’s included (high level)
- New concept page explaining the three tiers: fast, standard, cost-efficient
- Config reference updates for the request/route config surface to include batching_tier
- End-to-end examples (curl + SDK snippets) for setting batching_tier
- Trade-offs section (p95/p99 vs $/token vs GPU util) and which workloads each tier fits
- Streaming-specific behavior notes (token cadence sensitivity, why fast is default for streaming-heavy apps in beta)
- FAQ + migration guidance:
  - migrating from explicit batching knobs to tiers
  - precedence rules (explicit overrides win)
  - how to debug using the effective-config explain endpoint
  - common pitfalls (timeouts, overload protection interactions, long-context spikes)
- Observability section: what graphs to watch and what indicates a bad tier fit (queue delay distribution, cancellation rate, decode latency, etc.)

Customer-facing tier definitions (docs wording)
- fast: prioritize responsiveness and steady streaming cadence; conservative queue delay; lower batch aggregation; typical for interactive chat + streaming UIs.
- standard: balanced default; moderate batching to improve $/token while holding reasonable p95; recommended starting point for most non-streaming routes.
- cost-efficient: maximize throughput / minimize $/token; allows higher batching and queue delay; best for offline/batch jobs, summarization pipelines, and async workloads; requires tighter timeout alignment + monitoring.

Important: Docs avoid hard-coding numeric p95 targets because actual latency depends on model/SKU/context length; instead we explain relative behavior and point to “SLO tiers” and Console dashboards for measured performance. We do include queue-delay guardrail language (e.g., “bounded queue delay” and “overload protection may shed load earlier”) and clearly call out that streaming workloads are sensitive.

API / config examples included
- Hosted API request parameter:
  - batching_tier: "fast" | "standard" | "cost_efficient"
- Route-level config example (Console / config export) showing:
  - route.batching_tier set, with explicit knobs overriding as needed
- Private (Helm) example values snippet:
  - inference.defaults.batchingTier: standard
  - plus note on feature flag gating for beta

Precedence / migration guidance (as documented)
1) Explicit batching knobs (e.g., max_batch_size, max_queue_delay_ms, scheduler weights) always take precedence over batching_tier.
2) If batching_tier is set and explicit knobs are not, Redwood computes tier defaults based on workload signals and model/GPU family.
3) If neither is set, behavior remains unchanged unless the account/model/region is included in the staged rollout that enables standard tier defaults (beta).

Effective configuration (“what am I actually running?”)
- Added a small section describing the explain/effective-config endpoint that returns the computed defaults + sources (tier vs explicit override). This is intentionally framed as “for debugging” with a pointer to Console once the UI lands (ENG-18425).

Observability / troubleshooting guidance
- What to watch during tier changes:
  - queue_delay_ms histogram (p50/p95/p99)
  - batch_size distribution + batch formation rate
  - request latency by stage (prefill/decode) where available
  - timeout + cancellation rate
  - streaming: tokens/sec and inter-token gap (cadence)
- Common failure modes documented:
  - cost-efficient tier increases queue delay enough to hit client timeouts (fix: align timeouts, consider standard, confirm overload protection)
  - long-context prompts reduce batching effectiveness and can increase tail latency; consider fast/standard + cap context for interactive
  - mixed streaming/non-streaming on same route: choose fast or split routes

Docs IA changes (where pages live)
- Adds a new “Performance & Cost” subsection page for Batching Profiles / Tiers
- Updates existing “Configuration Reference” pages to cross-link to the tiers doc
- Adds FAQ page under “Troubleshooting” and links from the main tiers page

Commit summary
1) docs: add batching tiers concept page + trade-offs
2) docs: add config examples (curl/python/ts) for batching_tier
3) docs: add FAQ + migration guide + troubleshooting section
4) docs: add observability page and dashboard pointers
5) chore: update sidebar + redirects

Screenshots / preview
- Netlify preview: included in CI artifact “docs-preview” (see Checks). Key pages validated:
  - /performance/batching-tiers
  - /performance/batching-tiers/faq
  - /guides/migrating-to-batching-tiers

Reviewer notes / open questions addressed
- Naming: we consistently use “cost-efficient” in headings and “cost_efficient” only in config/code examples. (Per product thread, avoid “eco” naming.)
- Streaming: docs now explicitly recommend fast tier for streaming-heavy interactive workloads during beta and call out cadence risk; includes a “don’t do this” example (cost-efficient + strict 10s gateway timeout).
- Precedence rules: added a callout box and a small truth table to reduce confusion; also explicitly references SUP-18510.
- Model-specific behavior: avoided presenting tier settings as universal; added “model family / GPU SKU may adjust exact defaults” note and directs customers to effective-config output.

Checklist
- [x] Product sign-off on customer-facing wording (Aditya)
- [x] DevEx sign-off on examples (Alex)
- [x] Runtime sign-off on accuracy around scheduling/queue delay (Sofia)
- [x] Observability sign-off on metrics names/wording (Allison)
- [x] Links validated, redirects added, preview verified

Review conversation (selected)
- Alex Martinez: “Examples look good; can we show both per-request and per-route?”
  - Elliot Price: “Added per-route snippet under Route config and kept per-request for quickstart/curl.”
- Sofia Ivanova: “Please avoid implying max_queue_delay is fixed per tier; it’s workload-aware.”
  - Elliot Price: “Updated wording to ‘bounded queue delay’ + ‘computed defaults vary by model/workload’, and added effective-config section.”
- Allison Grant: “Metric naming: use queue_delay_ms not queue_wait_ms, and call out histogram quantiles.”
  - Elliot Price: “Updated all references and added a short glossary; linked to metrics page.”
- Aditya Rao: “We should be explicit that explicit knobs override tier; that was a major source of confusion.”
  - Elliot Price: “Added precedence callout + migration section + FAQ entry: ‘Why didn’t my tier change anything?’.”

- typecheck: pass
- docs-preview (Netlify): pass

Merge
Squash merged into main for inclusion in the beta docs rollout; coordinated with runtime-1.21 release notes workstream (Connor O’Brien).
